fields.description:
## Who benefits
Data scientists get a predictable, supported workflow for Lanternfish telemetry, with fewer hand-offs and less time spent on one-off fixes. SRE teams gain visibility into how Lanternfish telemetry behaves across teams, which today requires asking around or reading logs.
Today, teams that need Lanternfish telemetry assemble it themselves from scripts and internal notes; the result differs per team, is hard to support, and breaks on upgrade.

## Goal
Make Lanternfish telemetry usable by data scientists in day-to-day work, so that SRE teams no longer depend on manual workarounds.

## Scope
- A rollback path within one release
- Per-team quotas and limits
- An upgrade path with no manual steps
- Dashboards for the key health signals

## Success criteria
- Median setup time below 15 minutes for a new team.
- At least 3 internal teams onboarded within one release.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A rollback path within one release is verified.
- [ ] Per-team quotas and limits is verified.
- [ ] An upgrade path with no manual steps is verified.
fields.summary: [SYNTH] Fleet-wide inference telemetry with Lanternfish

fields.description:
## Problem
Operators of predictive model-serving endpoints cannot connect a slow client request to what happened inside the model server. MLServer already creates a server span for each REST request (its bundled FastAPI OpenTelemetry instrumentation), but on the platform those spans go nowhere: the exporter is hard-coded to an insecure connection, nothing configures it, and incoming trace context from the caller is not joined.

## Who benefits
- Platform operators diagnosing slow requests on predictive InferenceServices served by MLServer.
- Application teams that already trace their own services and want the model call in the same trace.

## Goal
For an InferenceService that opts in, each sampled REST inference request served by the MLServer runtime produces an MLServer server span that joins the caller's W3C trace context and is exported over TLS to the platform's existing data-science-collector, which already forwards traces to Tempo. One trace then shows the caller's spans and the time spent inside the model server.

## Scope
- Runtime: MLServer only, the supported MLServer ServingRuntime image, RawDeployment mode.
- Protocol: REST (KServe v2 HTTP) only.
- Workers: spans from the main MLServer process; with parallel workers enabled, inference inside a worker process is covered by the server span only (see P1 below).

## Requirements
| ID | Requirement | Acceptance | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Opt in per InferenceService with an annotation; odh-model-controller sets the OTEL_* environment (endpoint, sampler, resource attributes) on the predictor only when it is present | Without the annotation the predictor pod spec is byte-for-byte unchanged | P0 |
| R2 | MLServer exports spans over TLS, trusting the OpenShift service CA from the namespace's injected service-CA ConfigMap (downstream patch to the hard-coded insecure exporter) | Spans reach the collector on 4317 with TLS verification on; a wrong CA produces no export and no request errors | P0 |
| R3 | The server span joins an incoming W3C traceparent | A request sent with a traceparent appears in Tempo as a child of the caller's span | P0 |
| R4 | Parent-based ratio sampling, default 1 percent, set per InferenceService by the annotation value | Measured export rate within 0.5 percentage points of the configured ratio over 10,000 requests | P0 |
| R5 | The collector NetworkPolicy admits OTLP only from predictor pods (KServe predictor pod label), and the existing k8sattributes and identity-sanitizing processors set the namespace attribute | A pod without the label cannot export; a span claiming another namespace is rewritten to its real one | P0 |
| R6 | Separate inference span inside parallel-worker processes (trace context across MLServer's worker IPC) | Server span minus inference span equals codec and queue time within 1 ms | P1 |

## Non-functional requirements
- Overhead: at 1 percent sampling, added p95 latency below 2 ms in the benchmark below.
- Privacy: no request or response payload, header value or token in any span attribute.
- Availability: if the collector is unreachable or the CA is wrong, requests succeed unchanged and spans are dropped.

## Benchmark
The scikit-learn iris model on the MLServer runtime, one replica, 100 requests per second of KServe v2 REST for 10 minutes, measured with and without the annotation at 1 percent sampling and at 100 percent sampling. The p95 difference at 1 percent is the overhead figure. Owned by the model serving team; the harness is a small addition to the existing runtime performance tests.

## Out of scope
- Spans for the OpenShift router and the kube-rbac-proxy (or Authorino) authentication hop: that time appears only as the gap between the caller's span and the server span.
- gRPC: it is not externally routable on the predictive Route path today.
- LLMInferenceService, vLLM, OpenVINO Model Server, Triton and AutoGluon: each would be its own Initiative.
- The KServe agent sidecar and any proxy or Service rewiring.
- Installing or configuring the OpenTelemetry or Tempo operators: RHOAI does not install external operators; without the collector, nothing is exported.
- Per-namespace trace access for model owners: traces land in the shared Tempo, and access is arranged by administrators. Self-service access is a follow-on.

## Dependencies
- The existing data-science-collector deployment (OTLP over TLS on 4317) and its Tempo export.
- MLServer's bundled OpenTelemetry SDK and FastAPI instrumentation (already in the shipped image).
- One downstream MLServer patch (R2); no upstream change is needed for the P0 scope.

## Effort and rollout
- Size M: model serving team (odh-model-controller annotation and env injection, MLServer patch, benchmark) and platform observability team (NetworkPolicy, sanitization tests). About three sprints for both teams in parallel.
- Technology preview behind the annotation in one release; general availability after one release of preview feedback, with R6 considered for GA.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] R1-R5 pass on a cluster with the collector installed; R6 is tracked separately.
- [ ] The benchmark shows added p95 latency below 2 ms at 1 percent sampling.
- [ ] An InferenceService without the annotation is unchanged (pod spec diff and benchmark).
- [ ] With the collector absent or the CA wrong, all requests succeed and no errors are logged per request.
